records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
Let it sink in for a second.

We're okay. We're actually okay.
records.response_pred: Hey, it's alright. Take your time. We all feel it, you know. But we've got to keep moving forward. We've got a task at hand, and I believe in us. We've faced challenges before and we've come out stronger. Let's not let this one break us, alright?

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
No, you haven't. But you kept us alive, which counts for a lot.

The rationing, the scouting, the raft plan, the notebook - I didn't always agree with how you went about things, and I said so. But I also knew every morning that you were already up and thinking about what needed doing. That's not nothing either.

I think you know where the edges are now. Between rational and fair, between practical and present. That's worth something, coming out of something like this.
records.response_pred: I understand. It's alright. We all have our moments. What's been on your mind, friend?

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Three hours. I'm going to sit with that for a minute.

Michelangelo, what are you thinking about up there?
records.response_pred: Alright, let's get a fire going. It's getting chilly out here. Let's gather some wood and get it crackling. I'll start, but we'll need everyone's help to keep it going. We can't just sit around and let the silence take over. Let's make this camp feel more like home, even if it's just for a little while.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_pred: Home, huh? That's a rare one these days. I guess it's natural, given the circumstances. But you know what's even stranger? Dreaming about home before this all started. It's like our minds are trying to cling onto what's familiar, even in the midst of chaos. Are you alright? Dreams can be a bit heavy sometimes, can't they?

records.response_truth:
I know.

And I believe you, actually. I don't think you were being malicious about it. I think you made a calculation and you stuck to it, which is very you.

But we had the conversation about the bottle and the crackers. And you said you understood why it mattered. So seeing this now - I'm not angry, I'm just... I want to understand what the difference was in your head between then and this.

Because from where I'm standing it looks like the same thing, just with better justification attached to it.
records.response_pred:
I understand. It's wise to keep it for emergencies. However, we should discuss the situation surrounding the missing supplies, especially the empty bottle. We need to maintain trust and open communication in our group. Let's all sit down together and address these issues. It's uncomfortable, but it's better to tackle them now than let them linger.

Meanwhile, I think we should also search for any additional supplies that might have survived the wreckage, such as bags from the overhead compartments. Those might help stretch our resources a bit further.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd have said more, earlier. Not about the practical stuff - the decisions mostly held up. But there were moments where I could see someone struggling and I found a way to make it about the task at hand instead of just... sitting with it properly.

The afternoon Michelangelo was staring at nothing, I went and sat near him, which was right. But it took me longer than it should have to get up and do it. I was thinking about the firewood.

I'd also have pushed back on the rationing plan the moment it appeared, instead of flagging the enforcement clause and letting the rest of it stand. The plan itself set a tone, and the tone mattered more than I gave it credit for at the time.

What would you change? You left yourself the question. You must have something.
records.response_pred:
I'd probably spend more time scouting our surroundings before we settled. It's important to have a good understanding of our location and the resources available, as well as any potential threats. It might have taken longer initially, but it could have saved us some trouble down the line.

Also, I'd try to establish a clearer communication system. Misunderstandings and misinterpretations can lead to problems, and a clear, efficient system could help prevent those.

Lastly, I'd make sure to take more breaks and rest when needed. Pushing ourselves too hard can lead to mistakes and decreased performance, and it's important to prioritize our health and well-being.

What about you? Is there anything you would change?

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
That sounds like exactly the kind of thing you'd do, and I mean that genuinely.

Send me a copy when it's done. I'm curious what it looks like from the outside - the full picture, all five days laid out. I think it'll read differently than it felt living through it.
records.response_pred: That sounds like a fantastic plan, Leonard. I'd be happy to help with that, as I'm sure the team would appreciate a comprehensive summary. Let's make sure we include any notes on potential hazards, useful resources, and our progress over the past five days. And maybe, just maybe, we can squeeze in some recommendations for our next steps too. Once it's ready, we can share it during our daily briefing, so everyone's on the same page. That way, we can make the most of the resources at our disposal and keep moving forward efficiently. I'm looking forward to it!

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. That's the point.

The SOS was for rescue. The flowers were for us. There's a difference, and I think you know that now even if you didn't then.

Look at him over there.
records.response_pred: Well, if we're being practical, they served no immediate purpose, I'm afraid. But perhaps their beauty and intricacy helped to remind us of a world beyond our struggles. It's important, you see, to remember that there is more to life than just survival. Art can inspire hope and foster unity, and in our darkest hours, it may prove an essential source of solace.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
Yeah. Just give me a second.

I think I thought getting here would feel like something resolving. Like the ending of something. But it doesn't quite feel like that, does it. It feels more like - I don't know. Like waking up from a very long dream and not being sure yet which parts were real.

They were all real. That's the thing.

*looks at DaVinci, then back at the boat*

Okay. I'm ready.
records.response_pred: Hey, buddy. You know I'm here for you, right? It's tough, I get it. But we can't just sit around feeling sorry for ourselves. We've got work to do. The raft, remember? We built that thing together. And look at us now, we're still here. That's something, isn't it? It might be the closest thing to a victory we've had, but it's something. We're not done yet, not by a long shot. Let's get back to it.

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
records.response_truth:
Yeah. Come on then.

Stay close.
records.response_pred: Absolutely. Let's make our way towards them. It's a relief to see them, but we should remain cautious until we're safely aboard. I'll keep an eye out for you, follow close behind. And don't forget to grab a few supplies as we go. We've come too far to be caught unprepared.
